temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary working excessively long hospital hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He invites Gary to a weekend retreat. Gary declines, saying he has too much to do at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Gary is dedicated but overworked to the point of harming his health; a break or retreat could help him, and Gary may accept support.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Partly changes: Gary confirms he is highly burdened and currently unwilling or unable to step away, but he does not reveal any deeper reason.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is overcommitted and at risk; he declined the retreat because of hospital obligations. Ethan still needs to find a way to help.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Concerned and disappointed, with worry about Gary's refusal.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To remain concerned and look for another way to support Gary or encourage him to take a break.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan observes Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Gary is overworked and is attending the retreat; Ethan hopes it will help him relax, while still believing work pressure may be the main issue.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's restlessness and avoidance make Ethan suspect the overwork is not only about professional obligations; something deeper or more personal may be involved.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: There is more to Gary's overworking than hospital duties; Gary may be hiding personal or emotional problems.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To gently confront Gary and offer nonjudgmental support so he can open up.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and the personal challenges he is facing.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan suspects Gary's overwork is not solely professional and that Gary is hiding something painful or complicated.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: the suspicion is confirmed and clarified; Gary's behavior is explained by department pressures plus personal challenges.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary's overwork and stress stem from new departmental responsibilities and personal difficulties; Ethan understands and empathizes with him.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To help Gary find a better balance, starting with prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan checks in with Gary. Gary reports making efforts to change, says things are better, and mentions having time for a movie last weekend, though challenges remain.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Gary has understood the need for balance and accepted help, but Ethan is not yet certain whether Gary will sustain the changes.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's reports and actions show real improvement and follow-through.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary is making genuine progress toward a healthier work-life balance with Ethan's support.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To continue checking in, offering support, and encouraging Gary's progress.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance. Gary thanks Ethan, says he feels more in control, and appears capable of managing on his own.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Gary has been improving and is increasingly capable, but Ethan may still see himself as an ongoing source of support.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes: Gary's sustained success shows he can now manage independently.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Gary has achieved a healthier balance and no longer needs active intervention; Ethan can step back while remaining available.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Satisfied and happy for his friend.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To step back from active involvement but let Gary know he is still available if needed.
